title: Sell Mineral Rights in Fairdale, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Fairdale, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Fairdale, Greene County? Core Marcellus wet-gas country with heavy EQT activity. We buy — honest numbers, no pressure to sell.
heroLead: Fairdale sits in the richest part of the Marcellus wet-gas fairway in the whole state, farm country that EQT has drilled hard for over a decade.
intro: Fairdale is a rural Greene County community in the deepest, most liquids-rich stretch of the Marcellus play in Pennsylvania. Farm families here have generally had gas leases in place for years, with real production history behind most of the active wells nearby.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Fairdale, whether you're holding a producing interest, a leased tract waiting on development, or a fractional share from a family farm.

sections.heading: The deep core of the play
paragraphs: Greene County sits where the Marcellus is thickest and richest in the state, and Fairdale-area acreage has generally seen strong development activity from EQT as a result. That density typically means better production history to evaluate than in thinner parts of the play.

sections.heading: Pooled units and family farm acreage
paragraphs: Given how large modern spacing units are in this area, a single family farm near Fairdale is often just one piece of a much larger drilling unit, with royalty paid proportionate to acreage contributed rather than tied to any one specific well pad.

sections.heading: What drives value here
paragraphs: Well performance, your proportionate share, remaining lease term, and post-production deduction terms all factor into an offer, and we review your actual documents before naming a number.
We'll walk you through exactly how we arrived at any number, including how your unit's performance compares to typical activity in this part of Greene County.

faqs.question: Why is Fairdale considered such strong Marcellus territory?
faqs.answer: It sits in the deepest, most liquids-rich part of the wet-gas fairway in the state, which has generally supported stronger well performance than thinner parts of the play — though this describes the play generally, not a promise for any specific well.

faqs.question: My Fairdale-area farm is part of a large pooled unit. How does that affect my royalty?
faqs.answer: Your royalty is based on your proportionate share of the total unit acreage, so the unit's overall performance and your specific ownership percentage both matter.

faqs.question: Do you buy fractional interests from Greene County farm families?
faqs.answer: Yes, fractional interests inherited among multiple family members from a single farm are common in this area, and we regularly buy an individual heir's share.

faqs.question: Do EQT units near Fairdale typically include multiple adjoining farms?
faqs.answer: Yes, modern spacing units in this part of Greene County commonly pool several adjoining farms together, so your specific tract's acreage relative to the whole unit determines your proportionate royalty share.
